title: An eUTxO vault standard plus automated liquidity management
why: Ethereum has ERC-4626; Cardano has no shared vault interface. LP positions on Minswap, Splash and SundaeSwap are managed by hand, and the PRIME audit lists automated liquidity management and vault standards among its named gaps.
who: Liquidity providers, DAO treasuries, Liqwid/Indigo (yield-bearing receipt tokens as collateral)
funding: Cardano PRIME RFP (lending & vault standards; liquidity tooling)

title: Curated, isolated money markets on USDCx (Morpho-style)
why: Lending is pooled (Liqwid) or small (Surf, FluidTokens P2P). There is no risk-curator model, and the PRIME audit asks for a second independent price feed alongside Pyth.
who: USDCx holders looking for yield; risk curators; protocols needing credit lines
funding: Cardano PRIME RFP (curated lending; second price feed)
difficulty: Hard — oracle and liquidation design, audit

title: A shared batcher / solver network for orders and intents
why: Every DEX runs its own batcher, which fragments liquidity and trust. The DeFi Kernel open standard exists, but its treasury request failed, so nobody runs a neutral solver market.
who: DEXes that want to stop running batchers; solvers and market makers
difficulty: Medium–hard — off-chain infra plus economic design

title: BTC-ready credit and yield products
why: No trust-minimised BTC bridge is in production yet. Bifrost is on testnet and Pogun targets mid-December 2026. Products built now against iBTC and fBTC interfaces would be ready when a bridge lands.
who: BTC holders who want yield without selling; protocols bootstrapping BTC liquidity
funding: Cardano PRIME; Orion Fund for venture-scale teams
difficulty: Hard — say plainly which trust model you're using

title: A DeFi Gateway SDK with custody adapters
why: Named in Appendix C of the PRIME proposal. Institutions and fintechs need one API that reaches Cardano DeFi through Fireblocks-style custody, and none exists.
who: Exchanges, fintechs, custodians and market makers entering through Critical Integrations

title: Prediction markets
why: The category is effectively empty on DefiLlama (Bodega ≈ $0). eUTxO order-book patterns fit naturally: every position can be its own UTxO.
difficulty: Medium — the hard part is resolution and liquidity

title: Dual-stack wallets: MetaMask-controlled Cardano accounts
why: There is no EVM compatibility (Milkomeda shut down in 2025). FluidTokens has shown that an Aiken contract can let a MetaMask or Bitcoin wallet control a Cardano address, but it's a prototype, not a product.
who: EVM users arriving through USDCx and LayerZero; wallets that want new users
funding: Cardano PRIME RFP (dual-stack wallets; EVM→Cardano bridge)

title: Gasless onboarding: apps that pay users' fees
why: New users must get ADA before they can do anything, and every output needs min-ADA. Fee tanks exist (Aquarium), but there's no drop-in kit for app developers.
who: Consumer apps, games, loyalty programs like Barça Fan Lab
funding: Catalyst (next round); Cardano PRIME if it drives DeFi usage

title: A token analytics API and dashboard to replace TapTools
why: TapTools wound down in June 2026 after its leadership left, taking with it the API many wallets and bots used for prices, holders and charts.
who: Wallets, trading bots, portfolio apps, researchers
funding: Treasury or Intersect budget (public good); paid API

title: Dune dashboards and on-chain attribution for DeFi incentives
why: PRIME pays a performance fee only against verified TVL growth and wants action-based incentive campaigns with on-chain attribution. That needs neutral, reproducible dashboards.
who: Cardano PRIME, protocols applying for incentives, DReps

title: Transaction-building and debugging tools
why: The 2025 Cardano developer survey names off-chain transaction building, script-failure debugging and fragmented tooling as top pain points. CBOR inspection, budget profiling and readable script errors are still rough.
funding: Intersect Maintainer Retainer; Intersect budget process

title: A structured opportunity feed (bounties, RFPs, jobs)
why: Opportunities are scattered across forums, X and job boards. A volunteer compiles a weekly digest by hand, and three bounty boards are competing in early stages.
who: Builders looking for work; programs looking for applicants
blocks: The JSON behind this site's opportunity board
difficulty: Easy — the hard part is keeping it current

title: Agent wallets with spending policies
why: There's no CIP or product for an AI-agent wallet with daily limits, allowlists and human approval above a threshold. Today agents use hot wallets in the Masumi node or plain SDK wallets.
who: Masumi agents, x402 clients, anyone letting an LLM spend money
funding: Catalyst (next round); a strong CIP candidate

title: A production x402 facilitator and paid-API kit on mainnet
why: The Cardano x402 scheme is in the spec and on npm, but the Cardano Foundation facilitator has only been proven on Preprod.
who: API sellers, agent builders, data providers

title: An NFT marketplace and creator tooling after JPG Store
why: JPG Store, the main NFT marketplace, shut down on 23 May 2026. Collections and creators still exist, and CIP-68 metadata plus native assets make the contracts simpler than on most chains.
who: Existing collections, creators, games, ticketing and loyalty programs
difficulty: Medium — the hard part is liquidity and curation

title: Verifiable credentials and loyalty for brands
why: Barça Fan Lab proves the demand. Most brands need a white-label kit: sign in, get a wallet, earn credentials. Midnight adds the option of proving facts without revealing data.
funding: Catalyst (identity was a Pilot theme); CF Cardano Accelerator Program (real-world trust)
